title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel calls with result injection and retryable semantics
author: Ariella Chen
description: Motivation: customers are building multi-tool workflows that require deterministic injection of tool outputs back into the model context, safe parallel tool invocation, and retry semantics that preserve end-to-end correctness. This PR adds API-level ergonomics and runtime support for: 1) explicit tool result injection points so callers can opt into streaming a tool result back into the model as either a soft hint or a hard tokenized insertion, 2) parallel tool invocation primitives with per-tool isolation and backpressure-aware concurrency limits, 3) idempotent retry policies and observability hooks so transient tool failures can be retried without double-injecting results, and 4) OpenAI-compat shim improvements to preserve backwards compatibility for existing tool-calling patterns. Summary of changes: - API: extend the existing tool-calling shape with optional fields "injection_mode" (values: HINT|INJECT), "injection_token_limit" and "retry_policy" (values: NONE|TRANSIENT_RETRY|FORCE_RETRY) and a new response wrapper "tool_execution_metadata" that includes stable execution_id and attempt_count. - Server runtime: implement ParallelToolExecutor with per-request concurrency budget and KV-namespace isolation; add ToolExecutionCoordinator that serializes injection to the model context with dedup checks keyed by execution_id. - Retry semantics: add idempotency tokens and an attempt counter persisted in the coordinator; retries follow the configured retry_policy and update tool_execution_metadata so clients can reason about attempts. - Streaming: ensure streaming boundaries are respected when injection_mode==INJECT by buffering tool payloads until model insertion and emitting a single coherent insertion event; HINT mode streams partial outputs as model-prefixed messages. - OpenAI compatibility: update the /v1/compat/tools path to accept the new optional fields and map them to the internal execution model; keep previous behavior as default (INJECTION_MODE=HINT, RETRY_POLICY=NONE). Backwards compatibility: default behaviors preserve current semantics and the compatibility shim ensures older SDKs continue to work. Performance: added microbenchmarks and a stress test harness; measured <5% median token-latency regression for typical multi-tool workloads when concurrency is low and up to 15% improvement in overall throughput due to better parallelism when many independent tools are invoked. Testing: unit tests for coordinator, integration tests for injection dedup, e2e tests exercising retries and streaming transitions, and updated SDK examples. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated on a runtime flag "tool_exec_ergonomics_v2" for gradual exposure; start with Canary fleet then 100% ramp if metrics stable. See linked Linear tasks ENG-1245 ENG-1302 for rollout and monitoring dashboards.

review_comments: Marcus Patel: overall direction looks good. A couple of questions: 1) can you clarify the semantics of HINT vs INJECT for streaming clients? 2) how do we prevent duplicate side-effects when a tool is retried?

Ariella Chen (reply): HINT streams tool output into the assistant channel as context that the model may use but we do not insert tokens into the canonical user assistant token stream; INJECT performs a canonical insertion at a single point which is tokenized and visible to subsequent token generation. Duplicate side-effects are prevented via an execution_id persisted in the coordinator and by dedup checks at insertion time; see ToolExecutionCoordinator::commit_insertion.
Samir Gupta: CI flaked on the stress harness in first run; also please add a metric for execution_id collision rate
Ariella Chen (reply): fixed the race in coordinator shutdown and added collision_rate gauge; re-ran stress suite, attached results in CI comments.
Elena Rodriguez: request small API doc tweaks to call out that default retry policy is NONE for backwards compatibility; also can we add an example with two parallel unrelated tools?
Ariella Chen (reply): added doc snippet and SDK example demonstrating parallel calls to price_lookup and db_fetch with injection_mode=INJECT for price_lookup and HINT for db_fetch.
merge_summary: Merged by squash on 2025-11-18 after approvals from Marcus Patel and Elena Rodriguez. CI green. Rollout gated behind feature flag tool_exec_ergonomics_v2. No breaking changes to public API when flags off.
release_notes: Add optional tool-calling ergonomics: injection_mode, retry_policy, injection_token_limit, and improved parallel tool execution with idempotent retries and observability. Backwards compatible; feature gated behind tool_exec_ergonomics_v2.
